text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger, specifically noting when it started, if it is constant or intermittent, and what factors make it better or worse. Do you have any history of gout, diabetes, or recent injuries to that area?

text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the mechanism of injury from football suggests a traumatic event. Given the swelling and pain in the right ring finger, have you noticed any deformity, numbness, or tingling in that digit, and can you make a full fist?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: The inability to flex your right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint combined with pain and deformity suggests a potential mallet finger injury or a fracture. Did you hear a "pop" at the time of the injury, and can you extend your finger actively? REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Avulsion).

The history of forced flexion (finger caught and pulled), the inability to actively extend the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint, and the pain at that specific location are classic for a mallet finger. The X-ray I requested will confirm if there is an associated distal phalanx fracture. No further questions are needed; I am proceeding with this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation and imaging.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
